en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Mother of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
the Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the city of Vaiśālī together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus, including Śāriputra and others.
Furthermore, there was a great assembly of bodhisattvas,
such as Maitreya, who sat upon seats arranged for them, respectfully surrounding [the Buddha].
At that time, within the assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Samantabhadra.
Rising from his seat, he approached the World-Honored One;
baring his right shoulder and placing his right knee on the ground, he joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed him, saying: "World-Honored One."
There is a dhāraṇī of great clarity and profound phrases belonging to the Mother of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
which has been joyfully proclaimed by all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, present, and future.
When our Buddha, the World-Honored One, was a bodhisattva,
he also once proclaimed this dhāraṇī for the sake of seeking perfect, equal, and right enlightenment and for the benefit of sentient beings.
Furthermore, this dhāraṇī acts as both father and mother to those sons and daughters of good family who seek bodhisattvahood;
it is like a refuge for the orphaned and the solitary.
Those who lack mastery shall attain mastery.
If anyone recites this dhāraṇī and, having mastered it, upholds it,
all their sinful karma will be completely extinguished.
All practices and vows shall be brought to full completion;
even the cultivation of various great mantras shall attain accomplishment.
The Buddha addressed Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, saying:
It is exactly as you have said.
I recall that in the past,
when I was practicing as a bodhisattva.
In order to seek perfect, complete enlightenment,
he traversed immeasurable and boundless worlds as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā River.
Therein was a buddha-field named Sukhavatī.
In that land there is a Buddha named Amitāyus Tathāgata, Arhat,
Samyaksaṃbuddha. This Buddha Amitāyus currently exists,
constantly preaching the sublime Dharma to benefit sentient beings.
In that assembly, I was a brahmin named Īśvaraprabha.
At that time, I had already attained the Bhūmi of Radiant Illumination (Prabhākārī-bhūmi).
Within that assembly, I had previously proclaimed this dhāraṇī, the Mother of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, he shall bring great benefit to hundreds of thousands of nayutas of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.
Then, all the members of the great assembly in the gathering,
having heard this dhāraṇī, [were filled with joy].
All karmic offenses are completely extinguished,
and those who have not yet attained the knowledge of past lives acquire that knowledge.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, saying:
For the benefit of future beings in the degenerate age of the five turbidities,
may the sins of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who have committed the karma of the immediate retributions be extinguished.
In order that those who are solitary and destitute may have a refuge, I wish to joyfully proclaim and expound the *dhāraṇī* of the Mother of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Excellent, excellent! You may now proclaim it.
Having received the Buddha’s permission,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva then spoke the Mother Dhāraṇī of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: *Namaḥ bhagavate amitābhāya tathāgatāya*.
Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya.
Ṣaḍ-devī-namāḥ siddhārthāya īm-ariyāvairocani-svaramadan mahā-dhāraṇī-mantrapade sapravākṣa.
Yamīmi miṃ viśve 3. Mṛdāṃ tu 10. Tadyathā 11. Imi 12. Mire 13. Cire 14. Mire 15. Kuṇḍala 16. Kuṇḍale 17. Śrī 18. Svāhā.

Āḥ (28) yūhe (29) sāmānnaśani (30) nṛgamana-mānini (31) arya-nocana-puñji (32) sarva-vi... [The text provided ends here.]
Hūṃ na pra-viśaya-mi (33) sarva-hūṃ-ni-mi-śari svāhā (34). At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
if there are further people who receive and uphold this with a sincere heart,
all their karmic offenses shall be completely extinguished."
One shall always obtain protection during all times of fear.
If there are practitioners who wish to see me and the various siddhas,
they should apply themselves with diligence and without interruption.
If one recites with focused concentration three times each day for a full seven days,
I shall take pity on that person and manifest my own form before them.
Furthermore, if the practitioner continues to focus their mind in this manner...
If one recites silently with an uninterrupted mind for one month,
one shall obtain the manifestation of the true body of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, who will grant all requested vows,
and eventually attain the vision of Amitāyus Buddha.
Through the increase of extensive learning, one realizes the knowledge of past lives;
in whatever place one is born, one does not depart from the Buddha-dharma and possesses great wealth and honor,
even attaining the stage of non-retrogression.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, along with all the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas,
and the entire assembly, heard what the Buddha had taught.
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The *Buddha-spoken Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Mother of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*.
